newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Leadership change for British Tory Euro-MPs.
newsitem.headline: Leadership change for British Tory Euro-MPs.

text.p: Lord Plumb has stepped down as leader of the 18-member group of British Conservative Euro-MPs to be replaced by Tom Spencer, the group announced on Wednesday.
"We look forward to taking the fight into the Socialist camp both here in the European Parliament and back at home," Spencer said in a statement.
Caroline Jackson was elected as deputy chairwoman of the Conservative group.
The Socialist Group meanwhile re-elected British Labour MEP Pauline Green as its leader.
EP Prersident Klaus Haensch will be her deputy when his mandate expires at the end of next month.

Plumb announced in November he wanted to stand down as Conservative Euro-MP leader to concentrate on his post as co-president of the ACP-EU Joint Assembly during the forthcoming negotiations for a successor to the fourth ACP-EU Lome Convention.
The Joint Assembly brings together twice a year parliamentarians from the European Union and the 70 members of the African, Caribbean and Pacific group of countries.
Relations between the EU and the ACP group are governed by the Lome trade and aid convention, which is due to expire in the year 2000.
Britain's Conservative group has special status within the European Parliament.
Its 18 Euro-MPs are affiliated to the Christian Democrat European People's Party as individuals but not as a group.
